{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"The words settled into the dark.

Mara heard the watch ticking again. One beat. Then another, slow as a heart remembering how.

“Why?” she asked.

“I thought I could bring them back.”

A pale blue spark flickered in the key. It showed the stairs curling down into the tower’s belly, and Tomas standing several steps below her. His shadow still divided him: one shape clinging close, the other stretching upward along the wall.

“Who did you lose?” Mara asked.

Tomas’s silence told her.

The watch chimed. Its hands jerked backward, away from nine minutes past nine. Somewhere above, the gears answered with a groan. Dust drifted from the ceiling.

“You stopped it at the moment the bell rang,” she said. “That’s why the lane vanished.”

“And the faces,” Tomas whispered. “I thought they were only memories.”

The key warmed until its teeth bit into her palm. At the foot of the stairs stood a door she had never seen before, small and round, set into the stone like a porthole. A narrow slot ran across its center.

Behind it, someone began to sing.

Mara knew the tune. Their mother used to hum it while winding the kitchen clock, long before the tower, long before Tomas disappeared. The song stumbled over its final note, waiting.

“Don’t open that,” Tomas said.

“Is it her?”

“No.” His voice cracked. “It’s what the clock kept.”

The blue flame steadied. Mara turned the key in her fist and looked at the divided shadow.

“Then we’ll find out what it wants.”

She took the next step. The watch stopped ticking."}
